Business Entity Resolution — Exploratory Data Analysis[¶](#Business-Entity-Resolution-%E2%80%94-Exploratory-Data-Analysis)
==========================================================================================================================

### Amazon ML Challenge 2026[¶](#Amazon-ML-Challenge-2026)

Match business records across **3 independent sources** with no shared identifiers. For every **Source 1** entity, find all matching **Source 2 / Source 3** records. Scored by **macro-averaged F₀.₅** — precision weighted 2× over recall.

* * *

What this notebook establishes[¶](#What-this-notebook-establishes)
------------------------------------------------------------------

#

Finding

Why it matters

1

Every S2/S3 record belongs to **at most one** S1 entity

Turns the decision into a **global assignment problem** — the biggest precision lever available

2

Matches **never** cross country borders (100.0000%)

A **free, lossless** blocking key

3

**48%** of Source 1 records share a name with another record

Name alone cannot disambiguate — address is mandatory

4

The **address** is more reliable than the name

Name fails completely 3× more often

5

Address **rescues cross-script pairs** almost perfectly

Cross-script is a _scoring_ problem, not a blocking one

6

**Website domains** appear in S2/S3 only (4%), never S1

An undocumented noise class that zeroes token overlap

7

A **rare-token index reaches 99.78%** blocking recall

Name-only blocking would cap the score at 85%

Run top to bottom. Every number is computed from the competition data — nothing is hard-coded.

-----------------------

def thousands(x, \_\=None):
    if x \>= 1e6:  return f"{x/1e6:.1f}M"
    if x \>= 1e3:  return f"{x/1e3:.0f}k"
    return f"{x:.0f}"

def label\_bars(ax, bars, fmt\="{:,.0f}", pad\=0.01, horizontal\=True):
    """Direct value labels — the relief required by the palette contrast warning."""
    span \= (ax.get\_xlim()\[1\] if horizontal else ax.get\_ylim()\[1\])
    for b in bars:
        v \= b.get\_width() if horizontal else b.get\_height()
        if horizontal:
            ax.text(v + span\*pad, b.get\_y()+b.get\_height()/2, fmt.format(v),
                    va\="center", ha\="left", color\=INK2, fontsize\=9.5)
        else:
            ax.text(b.get\_x()+b.get\_width()/2, v + span\*pad, fmt.format(v),
                    ha\="center", va\="bottom", color\=INK2, fontsize\=9.5)

### Text helpers[¶](#Text-helpers)

Every read uses an explicit `sep="\t"`. Reading these files without it silently collapses each line into a single column — the most expensive five-second mistake available in this competition.

In \[2\]:

LEGAL \= {"inc","incorporated","corp","corporation","ltd","limited","llp","llc","pvt",
         "private","co","company","sarl","sas","sa","sci","gmbh","plc","and","the"}
PLACEHOLDER \= {"null","n/a","na","nan","nil","none","-",""}
DOMAIN\_RE \= re.compile(r"\\b\[\\w\\-\]+\\.(com|net|org|in|fr|co|io|biz|info)\\b", re.I)

INDIC \= \[("Devanagari",0x0900,0x097F), ("Bengali",0x0980,0x09FF), ("Gurmukhi",0x0A00,0x0A7F),
         ("Gujarati",0x0A80,0x0AFF), ("Oriya",0x0B00,0x0B7F), ("Tamil",0x0B80,0x0BFF),
         ("Telugu",0x0C00,0x0C7F), ("Kannada",0x0C80,0x0CFF), ("Malayalam",0x0D00,0x0D7F)\]

def script\_of(text):
    """Return the set of writing systems present in a string."""
    found \= set()
    for ch in text:
        cp \= ord(ch)
        if cp < 0x0500:
            continue
        for name, lo, hi in INDIC:
            if lo <= cp <= hi:
                found.add(name); break
    return found

def is\_latin(s):
    return all(ord(c) < 0x0500 for c in s if c.isalpha())

def norm(s):
    """Lowercase, strip accents and punctuation, collapse whitespace."""
    s \= unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", s)
    s \= "".join(c for c in s if not unicodedata.combining(c))
    s \= re.sub(r"\[^\\w\\s\]", " ", s.lower())
    return re.sub(r"\\s+", " ", s).strip()

def tokens(s, drop\_legal\=False):
    t \= \[w for w in norm(s).split() if w not in PLACEHOLDER\]
    return set(w for w in t if w not in LEGAL) if drop\_legal else set(t)

def trigrams(s):
    s \= re.sub(r"\[^a-z0-9\]", "", norm(s))
    return {s\[i:i+3\] for i in range(len(s)\-2)} if len(s) \>= 3 else {s}

def jaccard(a, b):
    return len(a & b) / len(a | b) if a and b else 0.0

def read\_head(path, n\=5):
    return pd.read\_csv(path, sep\="\\t", nrows\=n, dtype\=str, keep\_default\_na\=False)

1\. Dataset inventory[¶](#1.-Dataset-inventory)
-----------------------------------------------

One streaming pass over all seven files. Nothing is loaded into memory whole — at 2.35 GB a naive `read_csv` of everything would exhaust RAM on a 32 GB laptop.

In \[3\]:

FILES \= \[("train","train\_source1.tsv"), ("train","train\_source2.tsv"),
         ("train","train\_source3.tsv"), ("test","test\_source1.tsv"),
         ("test","test\_source2.tsv"),  ("test","test\_source3.tsv")\]

t0 \= time.time()
stats \= {}
for split, name in FILES:
    path \= (TRAIN if split\=="train" else TEST) / name
    countries, scripts \= collections.Counter(), collections.Counter()
    blank\_name \= blank\_addr \= domains \= placeholders \= n \= 0
    with open(path, encoding\="utf-8") as f:
        f.readline()
        for line in f:
            p \= line.rstrip("\\n").rstrip("\\r").split("\\t")
            if len(p) < 4:
                continue
            n += 1
            countries\[p\[3\]\] += 1
            sc \= script\_of(p\[1\])
            scripts\["Latin" if not sc else sorted(sc)\[0\]\] += 1
            if not p\[1\].strip(): blank\_name += 1
            if not p\[2\].strip(): blank\_addr += 1
            if DOMAIN\_RE.search(p\[1\]): domains += 1
            if any(c.strip().lower() in PLACEHOLDER and c.strip() for c in p\[2\].split(",")):
                placeholders += 1
    stats\[name\] \= dict(rows\=n, size\_mb\=path.stat().st\_size/1024/1024,
                       countries\=countries, scripts\=scripts, blank\_name\=blank\_name,
                       blank\_addr\=blank\_addr, domains\=domains, placeholders\=placeholders)
    print(f"  {name:<24} {n:\>10,} rows   ({time.time()\-t0:5.1f}s)")

inventory \= pd.DataFrame({
    "rows":        {k: v\["rows"\] for k,v in stats.items()},
    "size\_MB":     {k: round(v\["size\_mb"\],1) for k,v in stats.items()},
    "blank\_addr":  {k: v\["blank\_addr"\] for k,v in stats.items()},
    "domain\_names":{k: v\["domains"\] for k,v in stats.items()},
})
gt\_rows \= sum(1 for \_ in open(TRAIN/"train\_ground\_truth.tsv", encoding\="utf-8")) \- 1
inventory.loc\["train\_ground\_truth.tsv"\] \= \[gt\_rows,
    round((TRAIN/"train\_ground\_truth.tsv").stat().st\_size/1024/1024,1), 0, 0\]

3\. Country — and the France problem[¶](#3.-Country-%E2%80%94-and-the-France-problem)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Training data covers **US and India only**. The test set adds **France**, which appears nowhere in training. The spec is explicit: treat `country` as an _open set of string labels_, never hard-code `{US, India}`, and every test entity — France included — must appear in the submission.

In \[6\]:

4\. Ground truth structure[¶](#4.-Ground-truth-structure)
---------------------------------------------------------

How many records does a Source 1 entity actually match?

In \[7\]:

s1\_ids, s2\_refs, s3\_refs \= \[\], \[\], \[\]
c2\_list, c3\_list \= \[\], \[\]
with open(TRAIN/"train\_ground\_truth.tsv", encoding\="utf-8") as f:
    f.readline()
    for line in f:
        p \= line.rstrip("\\n").rstrip("\\r").split("\\t")
        if len(p) < 2: continue
        s1\_ids.append(int(p\[0\].split("-",1)\[1\]))
        a \= b \= 0
        for i in p\[1\].split(","):
            i \= i.strip()
            if not i: continue
            num \= int(i.split("-",1)\[1\])
            if i\[1\] \== "2": s2\_refs.append(num); a += 1
            else:           s3\_refs.append(num); b += 1
        c2\_list.append(a); c3\_list.append(b)

s2\_refs \= np.array(s2\_refs, dtype\=np.int64)

c2, c3  \= np.array(c2\_list, np.int32), np.array(c3\_list, np.int32)
total   \= c2 + c3

5\. ⭐ Finding 1 — every S2/S3 record belongs to at most ONE S1 entity[¶](#5.-%E2%AD%90-Finding-1-%E2%80%94-every-S2/S3-record-belongs-to-at-most-ONE-S1-entity)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If this holds, the problem is not independent per-pair classification. It is a **bipartite assignment problem**: when two S1 entities both claim the same S2 record, at most one can be right. Enforcing that constraint deletes a whole class of false positives _for free_ — exactly the error F₀.₅ weights double.

In \[9\]:

rows\_ \= \[\]
for label, refs in (("S2", s2\_refs), ("S3", s3\_refs)):
    uniq, counts \= np.unique(refs, return\_counts\=True)
    reused \= int((counts \> 1).sum())
    rows\_.append({"source": label, "references": len(refs), "distinct records": len(uniq),
                  "claimed by >1 entity": reused,
                  "max claims on one record": int(counts.max())})
constraint \= pd.DataFrame(rows\_).set\_index("source")
display(constraint)

n\_reused \= constraint\["claimed by >1 entity"\].sum()
total\_refs \= constraint\["references"\].sum()
if n\_reused \== 0:
    print(f"\\nZero reuse across all {total\_refs:,} references.")
    print("The S2/S3 side is strictly one-to-one -> enforce mutual exclusivity at decision time.")
else:
    print(f"\\n{n\_reused:,} records are claimed more than once.")

6\. A quarter of Sources 2 and 3 match nothing[¶](#6.-A-quarter-of-Sources-2-and-3-match-nothing)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Blocking will surface plenty of these. The matching model has to be comfortable rejecting **every** candidate for an entity.

In \[10\]:

def source\_ids(path):
    out \= \[\]
    with open(path, encoding\="utf-8") as f:
        f.readline()
        for line in f:
            i \= line.split("\\t",1)\[0\]
            if i: out.append(int(i.split("-",1)\[1\]))
    return np.array(out, dtype\=np.int64)

cov \= \[\]
for label, fname, refs in (("S2","train\_source2.tsv",s2\_refs), ("S3","train\_source3.tsv",s3\_refs)):
    allid \= source\_ids(TRAIN/fname)
    matched \= len(np.unique(refs))
    cov.append({"source": label, "records": len(allid), "matched": matched,
                "unmatched": len(allid)\-matched,
                "unmatched %": round(100\*(len(allid)\-matched)/len(allid), 2)})
    del allid
coverage \= pd.DataFrame(cov).set\_index("source")
display(coverage)

fig, ax \= plt.subplots(figsize\=(8.5, 2.9))
y \= np.arange(len(coverage))
ax.barh(y, coverage\["matched"\], color\=BLUE, height\=0.55, label\="matches an S1 entity",
        edgecolor\=SURFACE, linewidth\=2)
ax.barh(y, coverage\["unmatched"\], left\=coverage\["matched"\], color\=MUTED, height\=0.55,
        label\="distractor (matches nothing)", edgecolor\=SURFACE, linewidth\=2)
for i in range(len(coverage)):
    m  \= int(coverage\["matched"\].iloc\[i\])
    u  \= int(coverage\["unmatched"\].iloc\[i\])
    pc \= float(coverage\["unmatched %"\].iloc\[i\])
    ax.text(m/2, i, f"{m:,}", ha\="center", va\="center",
            color\="white", fontsize\=9.5, fontweight\="600")
    ax.text(m + u/2, i, f"{u:,}  ({pc:.0f}%)",
            ha\="center", va\="center", color\="white", fontsize\=9.5, fontweight\="600")
ax.set\_yticks(y, coverage.index); ax.set\_xticks(\[\]); ax.grid(visible\=False)
ax.set\_title("How much of each source is a distractor")

7\. Writing systems — Source 1 is Latin, Sources 2 and 3 are not[¶](#7.-Writing-systems-%E2%80%94-Source-1-is-Latin,-Sources-2-and-3-are-not)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Nine Indic scripts appear, all in India-labelled records. **Source 1 is 100% Latin**, so for those records the match is necessarily Latin → non-Latin.

They are _phonetic transliterations of English_, not translations:

Non-Latin

Reads as

`प्राइवेट लिमिटेड`

8\. Missing values — blanks _and_ literal placeholder strings[¶](#8.-Missing-values-%E2%80%94-blanks-and-literal-placeholder-strings)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Missing data is not only blank. It is also written out as text: `null`, `n/a`, `na`, `nan`, `nil`, `none`, `-`.

**Why this matters more than it looks:** left untreated, `null` becomes a _token that two unrelated addresses share_, inflating every token-overlap and TF-IDF similarity — manufacturing exactly the false merges F₀.₅ punishes hardest.

In \[12\]:

9\. Load a sample of real matched pairs[¶](#9.-Load-a-sample-of-real-matched-pairs)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Everything from here compares Source 1 records against their **true** matches. We sample ground-truth entities and pull only the records involved, keeping memory in the low hundreds of MB.

In \[13\]:

SAMPLE \= 120\_000
rng \= random.Random(0)

\# reservoir-sample ground-truth rows
rows\_gt \= \[\]
with open(TRAIN/"train\_ground\_truth.tsv", encoding\="utf-8") as f:
    f.readline()
    for k, line in enumerate(f):
        if len(rows\_gt) < SAMPLE:
            rows\_gt.append(line)
        else:
            j \= rng.randint(0, k)
            if j < SAMPLE: rows\_gt\[j\] \= line

wanted \= {1:set(), 2:set(), 3:set()}
gt \= \[\]
for line in rows\_gt:
    p \= line.rstrip("\\n").rstrip("\\r").split("\\t")
    if len(p) < 2: continue
    ids \= \[i.strip() for i in p\[1\].split(",") if i.strip()\]
    gt.append((p\[0\], ids)); wanted\[1\].add(p\[0\])
    for i in ids: wanted\[int(i\[1\])\].add(i)

recs, pool \= {}, {2: \[\], 3: \[\]}
t0 \= time.time()
for n in (1,2,3):
    with open(TRAIN/f"train\_source{n}.tsv", encoding\="utf-8") as f:
        f.readline()
        for k, line in enumerate(f):
            p \= line.rstrip("\\n").rstrip("\\r").split("\\t")
            if len(p) < 4: continue
            if p\[0\] in wanted\[n\]:
                recs\[p\[0\]\] \= (p\[1\], p\[2\], p\[3\])
            elif n in pool and len(pool\[n\]) < 60\_000 and k % 37 \== 0:
                pool\[n\].append((p\[0\], p\[1\], p\[2\], p\[3\]))   \# random negatives

print(f"sampled {len(gt):,} entities -> {len(recs):,} records loaded in {time.time()\-t0:.0f}s")
print(f"negative pool: {len(pool\[2\]):,} S2 + {len(pool\[3\]):,} S3 records")

sampled 120,000 entities -> 535,259 records loaded in 15s
negative pool: 60,000 S2 + 60,000 S3 records

for s1, ids in gt:

10\. ⭐ Finding 2 — matches never cross country borders[¶](#10.-%E2%AD%90-Finding-2-%E2%80%94-matches-never-cross-country-borders)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If this holds, `country` is a **free, lossless blocking key**: partition first, lose nothing, and cut the search space several-fold. It also works for France despite France being unseen, because a partition is not a learned feature.

In \[15\]:

country\_pairs \= collections.Counter(); script\_pairs \= collections.Counter()
name\_j, addr\_j \= \[\], \[\]
cross\_addr, same\_addr \= \[\], \[\]
exact\_name \= same\_tokens \= n\_pairs \= addr\_blank \= 0
zero\_name\_examples, cross\_examples \= \[\], \[\]

for s1, ids in gt:
    if s1 not in recs: continue
    n1, a1, c1 \= recs\[s1\]
    t1n, t1a, tri1 \= tokens(n1, True), tokens(a1), trigrams(n1)
    for i in ids:
        if i not in recs: continue
        n2, a2, c2 \= recs\[i\]
        n\_pairs += 1
        country\_pairs\[(c1, c2)\] += 1
        lat \= is\_latin(n2)
        script\_pairs\[lat\] += 1
        if norm(n1) \== norm(n2): exact\_name += 1
        t2n, t2a \= tokens(n2, True), tokens(a2)
        if t1n and t1n \== t2n: same\_tokens += 1
        nj, aj \= jaccard(t1n, t2n), jaccard(t1a, t2a)
        name\_j.append(nj); addr\_j.append(aj)
        if not t1a or not t2a: addr\_blank += 1
        (cross\_addr if not lat else same\_addr).append(aj)
        if not lat and aj \> 0.8 and len(cross\_examples) < 3:
            cross\_examples.append((s1, n1, a1, i, n2, a2, aj))
        if nj \== 0.0 and lat and len(zero\_name\_examples) < 8:
            zero\_name\_examples.append((n1, n2, aj))

same \= sum(v for (a,b), v in country\_pairs.items() if a \== b)
print(f"true pairs analysed : {n\_pairs:,}")
print(f"same country        : {same:,}  ({100\*same/n\_pairs:.4f}%)")
print(f"cross country       : {n\_pairs\-same:,}")
print()
print(f"cross-script pairs (Latin S1 -> non-Latin match): "
      f"{script\_pairs\[False\]:,} ({100\*script\_pairs\[False\]/n\_pairs:.2f}%)")

11\. ⭐ Finding 3 — how separable are true pairs from random pairs?[¶](#11.-%E2%AD%90-Finding-3-%E2%80%94-how-separable-are-true-pairs-from-random-pairs?)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The single most important question for the matching model. We compare true pairs against random **same-country** non-matches — the realistic hard case, since country already filters.

In \[16\]:

neg\_name, neg\_addr \= \[\], \[\]
by\_country \= collections.defaultdict(list)
for n in (2,3):
    for r in pool\[n\]: by\_country\[r\[3\]\].append(r)

tries \= 0
while len(neg\_name) < 60\_000 and tries < 400\_000:
    tries += 1
    s1, ids \= rng.choice(gt)
    if s1 not in recs: continue
    n1, a1, c1 \= recs\[s1\]
    cand \= by\_country.get(c1)
    if not cand: continue
    r \= rng.choice(cand)
    if r\[0\] in set(ids): continue
    neg\_name.append(jaccard(tokens(n1, True), tokens(r\[1\], True)))
    neg\_addr.append(jaccard(tokens(a1), tokens(r\[2\])))

def summarise(xs):
    xs \= np.sort(np.array(xs))
    return dict(n\=len(xs), p25\=np.percentile(xs,25), median\=np.median(xs),
                p75\=np.percentile(xs,75), zero\=100\*(xs\==0).mean())

sep \= pd.DataFrame({
    "name — TRUE":     summarise(name\_j),  "name — random":    summarise(neg\_name),
    "address — TRUE":  summarise(addr\_j),  "address — random": summarise(neg\_addr),
}).T
sep\["n"\] \= sep\["n"\].astype(int)
sep.columns \= \["pairs","p25","median","p75","zero-overlap %"\]
display(sep.round(3))

14\. ⚠️ Finding 6 — name ambiguity is the main precision risk[¶](#14.-%E2%9A%A0%EF%B8%8F-Finding-6-%E2%80%94-name-ambiguity-is-the-main-precision-risk)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If many Source 1 entities share a name, then name similarity alone **cannot** identify the right one — and a wrong pick is a false merge, the error F₀.₅ punishes at double weight.

In \[20\]:

name\_counts \= collections.Counter()
n1\_total \= 0
with open(TRAIN/"train\_source1.tsv", encoding\="utf-8") as f:
    f.readline()
    for line in f:
        p \= line.rstrip("\\n").rstrip("\\r").split("\\t")
        if len(p) < 4: continue
        n1\_total += 1
        name\_counts\[" ".join(sorted(tokens(p\[1\], True)))\] += 1

dupes  \= sum(v for v in name\_counts.values() if v \> 1)
groups \= sum(1 for v in name\_counts.values() if v \> 1)
print(f"Source 1 records                    : {n1\_total:,}")
print(f"distinct normalised names           : {len(name\_counts):,}")
print(f"records sharing a name with another : {dupes:,}  ({100\*dupes/n1\_total:.2f}%)")
print(f"ambiguous name groups               : {groups:,}")
print(f"largest group                       : {max(name\_counts.values()):,}")

top \= name\_counts.most\_common(10)
fig, (ax1, ax2) \= plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize\=(12.5, 4.0), gridspec\_kw\={"width\_ratios":\[1,1.4\]})

b2 \= ax2.barh(range(len(names\_)), vals\_, color\=SEQ\[4\], height\=0.62)

15\. ⭐ Finding 7 — blocking recall: the ceiling on everything[¶](#15.-%E2%AD%90-Finding-7-%E2%80%94-blocking-recall:-the-ceiling-on-everything)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Blocking sets a **hard ceiling** on final recall — a true match it never proposes is invisible to every downstream stage. We measure candidate recall for several strategies.

"Rare" = a token appearing in under 1% of records.

In \[21\]:

df\_tok \= collections.Counter(); n\_docs \= 0
for rid, (nm, ad, ct) in recs.items():
    if rid.startswith("S1-"): continue
    n\_docs += 1
    for t in tokens(ad) | tokens(nm, True): df\_tok\[t\] += 1
rare\_cut \= max(2, 0.01\*n\_docs)

hits \= collections.Counter(); totals \= 0
for s1, ids in gt:
    if s1 not in recs: continue
    n1, a1, c1 \= recs\[s1\]
    t1n, t1a, tri1 \= tokens(n1, True), tokens(a1), trigrams(n1)
    rare1 \= {t for t in (t1n|t1a) if df\_tok.get(t,0) < rare\_cut}
    for i in ids:
        if i not in recs: continue
        n2, a2, \_ \= recs\[i\]
        totals += 1
        t2n, t2a \= tokens(n2, True), tokens(a2)
        rare2 \= {t for t in (t2n|t2a) if df\_tok.get(t,0) < rare\_cut}
        tri\_ok \= jaccard(tri1, trigrams(n2)) \>= 0.2
        if t1n & t2n:                   hits\["shares ≥1 name token"\] += 1
        if t1a & t2a:                   hits\["shares ≥1 address token"\] += 1
        if (t1n & t2n) or (t1a & t2a):  hits\["name OR address token"\] += 1
        if rare1 & rare2:               hits\["shares ≥1 RARE token"\] += 1
        if tri\_ok:                      hits\["name trigram J ≥ 0.2"\] += 1
        if (rare1 & rare2) or tri\_ok:   hits\["RARE token OR trigram"\] += 1

recall \= pd.DataFrame(\[{"strategy": k, "recall %": round(100\*v/totals, 2)}
                       for k, v in hits.items()\]).sort\_values("recall %").set\_index("strategy")
display(recall)

fig, ax \= plt.subplots(figsize\=(10, 3.8))
cols\_ \= \[GOOD if v \>= 99 else (YELLOW if v \>= 95 else CRITICAL) for v in recall\["recall %"\]\]
b \= ax.barh(recall.index, recall\["recall %"\], color\=cols\_, height\=0.62)
ax.set\_xlabel("% of true matches the candidate set contains")
ax.set\_title("Blocking recall — the ceiling on final recall")
ax.set\_xlim(0, 108)
label\_bars(ax, b, fmt\="{:.2f}%")
ax.axvline(99, color\=INK2, linestyle\=":", linewidth\=1.2)
ax.grid(axis\="y", visible\=False)
plt.tight\_layout(); plt.show()

print(f"Name-only blocking discards {100\-recall.loc\['shares ≥1 name token','recall %'\]:.2f}% "
      "of all true matches before the model even starts.")
print(f"\\nEasy-half check: {100\*exact\_name/n\_pairs:.2f}% of true pairs match on the raw "
      f"normalised name; {100\*same\_tokens/n\_pairs:.2f}% have an identical token set once "
      "legal suffixes are dropped.")

16\. What this means for the pipeline[¶](#16.-What-this-means-for-the-pipeline)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#

Decision

Evidence

1

**Partition by country first**

100.0000% of matches are same-country — free, lossless

2

**Block on a rare-token inverted index over name ∪ address**

99.78% recall ceiling vs 85.09% for name-only

3

**Add a char-trigram pass**

catches the 4% domain-style names that token overlap misses

4

**Normalise before blocking**

legal suffixes, placeholder strings, domain splitting, Indic transliteration

5

**Score name AND address; allow "name 0 + address 1" to be a match**

that pattern is 7.2% of all true pairs

6

**Enforce one-to-one on the S2/S3 side at decision time**

zero records are shared between entities — free precision

7

**Cap at 5 from S2 and 6 from S3**

no entity in 2.2M ever exceeds those

8

**Be willing to predict nothing**

5.6% of entities are singletons, worth a full 1.0 each; ~26% of S2/S3 match nothing

### The metric drives the strategy[¶](#The-metric-drives-the-strategy)

F₀.₅ weights precision **2× over recall**. On a 2-match entity, one spurious extra scores **0.714** while one omission scores **0.833** — so when the model is uncertain, **predicting nothing beats guessing**. Because the average is _macro_ over entities, a mistake on a singleton costs exactly as much as a mistake on an 11-match entity.

### Biggest risks[¶](#Biggest-risks)

1.  **Name ambiguity** — 48% of Source 1 shares a name; leaning on name similarity produces confident wrong merges.
2.  **France** — 15% of the scored entities, zero training data. Nothing country-specific may be hard-coded, and a per-country threshold cannot be fitted for it.
3.  **Blocking recall** — invisible in the leaderboard score. Measure it every run.
